synthesis.content:
### Central insight
Start with unseen carbon in coastal soils, then connect storage to the consequences of habitat damage.

### Evidence
NOAA identifies sea grasses, mangroves and salt marshes as coastal sinks. Most of the carbon taken up by those ecosystems is stored below ground. Damage can release stored carbon back into the atmosphere.

### Gaps and uncertainty
Do not convert an account of storage into a quantified mitigation guarantee or claim all blue carbon is soil carbon.
